seeds.name: Tomato
seeds.soil: Well-drained, rich in organic matter, pH 6.0-6.8
seeds.effort_level: Moderate - needs staking, pruning suckers, consistent watering

growing_steps.step: Start seeds indoors in seed starting mix, 1/4 inch deep. Keep moist and warm (70-80°F).
Seeds should germinate. Move to bright light (grow light 14-16 hrs/day or sunny south window).
When seedlings have 2 sets of true leaves, transplant to larger pots (3-4 inch).
Begin hardening off — place outdoors in sheltered spot for increasing hours over 7-10 days.
Transplant outdoors after last frost. Plant deep (bury 2/3 of stem). Install cage or stake.
Fertilize with balanced fertilizer. Pinch off suckers growing in leaf axils for indeterminate varieties.
Flowers should appear. Ensure consistent watering to prevent blossom end rot.
First fruits ripening! Harvest when fully colored and slightly soft to touch.
Continue harvesting regularly to encourage more fruit production through the season.

tips: Bury stems deep when transplanting — roots grow from buried stem
Consistent watering prevents cracking and blossom end rot
Prune lower leaves to improve air circulation
library_resources: Seed library (many libraries carry tomato seeds)
Tomato cages (some tool libraries lend these)

seeds.name: Lettuce
seeds.space_needed: 1 sq ft per plant (or dense in containers)
seeds.water: 1 inch per week, keep soil consistently moist
seeds.effort_level: Low - one of the easiest crops to grow

growing_steps.step: Sow seeds on surface of moist soil, barely cover with 1/8 inch soil. Keep moist.
Seeds germinate quickly. Thin seedlings to 6-12 inches apart when 2 inches tall.
Keep soil consistently moist. Mulch around plants to retain moisture and keep roots cool.
Begin harvesting outer leaves for 'cut and come again' harvest. Plant grows new leaves from center.
Full heads ready for harvest. Cut at base or continue picking outer leaves.
Sow succession planting every 2 weeks for continuous harvest. Watch for bolting in heat.

tips: Grows great in containers and window boxes
Succession plant every 2 weeks for continuous harvest
Bolts (goes to seed) in hot weather — grow in partial shade in summer
library_resources: Seed library (lettuce seeds are commonly available)

seeds.name: Basil
seeds.water: 1 inch per week, keep evenly moist
seeds.effort_level: Low - pinch flowers to keep producing leaves

growing_steps.step: Start seeds indoors in moist seed starting mix. Press seeds into surface, cover lightly.
Seeds germinate. Provide bright light — south-facing window or grow light.
Transplant seedlings to individual pots when they have 2 sets of true leaves.
Harden off and transplant outdoors after last frost, or keep growing on sunny windowsill.
Begin harvesting! Pinch stems just above a leaf pair to encourage bushy growth.
Pinch off any flower buds to keep the plant producing flavorful leaves.
Continue harvesting regularly. Make pesto or dry leaves before first frost.

tips: Pinch off flower buds to extend harvest
Can grow indoors year-round on a sunny windowsill
Harvest from the top to encourage bushy growth

seeds.name: Pepper
seeds.effort_level: Moderate - needs warmth and patience, slow to start

growing_steps.step: Start seeds indoors in warm conditions (80-85°F). A heat mat helps significantly with germination.
Seeds germinate (peppers are slow!). Provide strong light — 14-16 hours under grow lights.
Transplant to 3-4 inch pots when seedlings have 2 sets of true leaves.
Begin hardening off plants. Peppers are very frost-sensitive — wait until nights stay above 55°F.
Transplant outdoors. Add support stake. Water deeply at planting.
Flowers appear. Avoid high-nitrogen fertilizer — switch to phosphorus-rich feed.
Peppers forming! Leave on plant until desired size and color for best flavor.
Harvest peppers by cutting (not pulling) from the plant. Regular harvest encourages more fruit.

tips: Heat mats dramatically improve germination
Pick first few flowers to strengthen the plant
Hot peppers get hotter with a bit of stress (less water near harvest)

seeds.name: Cucumber
seeds.water: 1-2 inches per week, consistent moisture critical
equipment: Trellis or tomato cage (for vertical growing)
Large pot (5+ gallon) or garden bed
seeds.effort_level: Low to Moderate - prolific once established

growing_steps.step: Direct sow outdoors after last frost (soil 60°F+), or start indoors 3 weeks before in peat pots.
Seeds germinate quickly. Keep soil moist but not waterlogged.
Thin to strongest seedling per spot. Install trellis for vertical growing.
Vines begin to run. Train onto trellis. Mulch heavily to retain moisture.
Flowers appear. Both male and female flowers are normal — female flowers have a tiny cucumber behind them.
First cucumbers forming! Water consistently — inconsistent water causes bitter fruit.
Harvest cucumbers when 6-8 inches (slicing) or 2-4 inches (pickling). Pick daily for best production.

tips: Grow vertically to save space and keep fruit clean
Harvest frequently — overripe cucumbers signal plant to stop producing
Bitter fruit usually means inconsistent watering

seeds.name: Carrot
seeds.sun: Full sun to partial shade (4-6 hours)
seeds.soil: Deep, loose, sandy soil free of rocks, pH 6.0-6.8
equipment: Garden bed or deep container (12+ inches)
seeds.effort_level: Low - direct sow and wait, minimal maintenance

growing_steps.step: Direct sow tiny seeds 1/4 inch deep in loose, rock-free soil. Keep surface moist — cover with burlap or row cover.
Be patient! Carrots are slow to germinate (14-21 days). Keep soil surface moist.
Seedlings emerge — thin to 2-3 inches apart. This is essential for proper root development.
Tops growing well. Keep soil evenly moist. Side-dress with compost.
Check root size by brushing soil from top of carrot. Harvest when shoulders are 1/2 to 3/4 inch.
Harvest by loosening soil with a fork first, then gently pulling. Carrots sweeten after light frost!

tips: Don't transplant — always direct sow
Rocks and hard soil cause forked roots
Short varieties like 'Little Finger' are great for containers

seeds.name: Green Bean
seeds.effort_level: Low - one of the easiest vegetables to grow

growing_steps.step: Direct sow seeds 1-2 inches deep after last frost when soil is warm (60°F+). Do not start indoors.
Seeds germinate in 4-10 days. Keep soil moist but not soggy.
For pole beans, install trellis or poles. Bush beans need no support.
Plants flowering. Avoid overhead watering during bloom to help pollination.
Beans ready to pick! Harvest when pods are firm and snap easily, before seeds bulge.
Pick every 2-3 days to keep plants producing. Bush beans produce for 2-3 weeks, pole beans all season.

tips: Don't start indoors — beans don't transplant well
Bush beans are easiest, pole beans produce longer
Pick regularly to keep plants producing

seeds.name: Strawberry
seeds.germination_days: 14-28 days (from seed; usually started from transplants)
seeds.days_to_harvest: 4-6 weeks from flowering (Year 2 for best harvest)
seeds.planting_depth: Surface sow (seeds need light to germinate)
equipment: Strawberry planter, hanging basket, or garden bed
seeds.effort_level: Low to Moderate - perennial, returns each year

growing_steps.step: Start seeds indoors (cold stratify first — freeze seeds for 2-4 weeks). Surface sow on moist soil.
Tiny seedlings emerge. Keep under grow lights 14-16 hours/day. Very delicate at this stage.
Transplant to individual pots when seedlings have 3+ true leaves.
Harden off and transplant outdoors after last frost. Mulch with straw.
Remove flowers the first year for June-bearing types to strengthen the plant for next year's harvest.
Runners appear — pin to soil to start new plants, or clip to focus energy on mother plant.
Year 2: Full harvest! Pick berries when fully red. Protect from birds with netting.

tips: Starting from transplants is much easier than seed
Straw mulch keeps berries clean and retains moisture
Pinch first-year flowers for bigger harvest in year two

seeds.name: Spinach
seeds.sun: Partial to full sun (3-5 hours ideal)
seeds.water: 1-1.5 inches per week, keep soil moist
seeds.effort_level: Low - cool season crop, very fast growing

growing_steps.step: Direct sow seeds 1/2 inch deep in cool soil (ideally 50-65°F). Can start as early as 4-6 weeks before last frost.
Seeds germinate in 5-14 days. Keep soil consistently moist.
Thin seedlings to 3-5 inches apart. Use thinnings as microgreens in salads!
Leaves growing quickly. Side-dress with nitrogen-rich fertilizer or compost tea.
Begin harvesting outer leaves when they're 3-4 inches long. Inner leaves continue growing.
Watch for bolting as temperatures rise above 75°F. Harvest entire plant before it bolts.

tips: Best grown in spring and fall — bolts in summer heat
Shade cloth extends the harvest in warmer weather
Succession plant every 2 weeks for continuous harvest

seeds.name: Radish
seeds.sun: Full sun to partial shade (4-6 hours)
equipment: Any container at least 6 inches deep
seeds.effort_level: Very Low - the fastest vegetable you can grow

growing_steps.step: Direct sow seeds 1/2 inch deep as soon as soil can be worked (even before last frost!).
Seeds germinate in just 3-5 days! Thin to 2 inches apart.
Keep soil evenly moist. Radishes grow fast — uneven water causes cracking.
Check size by brushing soil away from tops. Harvest when 1 inch in diameter.
Harvest promptly! Overgrown radishes become woody and pithy. Sow more seeds for next round.

tips: Fastest crop from seed to table — great confidence builder
Don't let them get too big or they become woody
Perfect companion plant — sow between slower crops
library_resources: Seed library (radish seeds are very common)

seeds.name: Mint
equipment: Container with drainage (ALWAYS use a container)
seeds.effort_level: Very Low - nearly impossible to kill, grows aggressively

growing_steps.step: Start seeds indoors — surface sow on moist soil (seeds need light). Or much easier: buy a starter plant.
Seeds germinate in 10-15 days. Keep soil moist. Provide bright indirect light.
Transplant to a dedicated container. ALWAYS grow mint in containers — it spreads aggressively in ground.
Begin harvesting! Cut stems just above a leaf pair. Plant bushes out from the cut point.
Pinch off flower buds to keep leaves flavorful. Harvest regularly to prevent legginess.
Plant is well-established. Harvest freely — it's very hard to over-harvest mint!

tips: ALWAYS grow in a container — mint is invasive in garden beds
Can grow indoors year-round
The more you harvest, the bushier it grows

seeds.name: Zucchini
seeds.water: 1-2 inches per week at base of plant
equipment: Large container (10+ gallon) or garden bed
seeds.effort_level: Low - incredibly productive, may produce more than you need!

growing_steps.step: Direct sow seeds 1 inch deep after last frost (soil 60°F+). Plant 2-3 seeds per spot.
Seeds germinate in 4-7 days. Thin to one strongest plant per spot.
Plants growing fast. Mulch around base to retain moisture and suppress weeds.
Large yellow flowers appear. Both male and female flowers are normal.
First zucchini forming! Harvest when 6-8 inches for best flavor and texture.
Check daily — zucchini grow FAST. A 6-inch zucchini can be a baseball bat by tomorrow!
Watch for powdery mildew on leaves. Improve air circulation and water at the base, not leaves.

tips: Harvest small (6-8 inches) for best flavor
One plant will feed a family — plant 2-3 max!
Check plants daily in peak season, they grow incredibly fast

seed_libraries.description: Many public libraries host seed libraries where you can check out seeds for free
seed_libraries.how_to_find: Ask your local library, search '[your city] seed library', or check seedlibraries.org
seed_libraries.what_to_expect: Free seed packets, usually heirloom and open-pollinated varieties adapted to your region

tool_libraries.description: Tool lending libraries let you borrow gardening tools you might not want to buy
tool_libraries.how_to_find: Search '[your city] tool library' or 'tool lending library near me'

growing_equipment.description: Some libraries and community organizations lend growing equipment
growing_equipment.how_to_find: Check library of things, community gardens, local garden clubs

knowledge_resources.description: Libraries offer extensive gardening knowledge resources

usda_zones.description: USDA Plant Hardiness Zones help determine when to plant based on your location
usda_zones.how_to_find: Enter your zip code at planthardiness.ars.usda.gov
